title: The Geometric Phase as a Diagnostic for Driven-Dissipative Oscillators
authors: Zeen Sun, Yuan Shen, Haitao Ding, Yuancheng Zhan, Leong-Chuan Kwek
abstract: Driven-dissipative quantum oscillators lock their phase, deform their limit cycles, and undergo dissipative phase transitions, yet these behaviors are read from unrelated quantities defined on the same steady-state density matrix. We show that a single geometric quantity organizes them. Winding the phase of the drive generates a closed loop of nonequilibrium steady states, and because the Liouvillian is covariant under number rotations, the kinematic mixed-state geometric phase of this loop reduces exactly to an eigensystem functional of a single steady state. Under weak driving, it is governed by the same nearest-neighbor coherences that produce phase locking and inherits the Arnold tongue of synchronization. Near the Hopf threshold, it registers the nonperturbative reorganization of the steady-state eigenvectors. And in the squeezing-driven Kerr resonator, it develops distinct signatures at the first and second order dissipative phase transitions. The geometric phase thus provides a unified and experimentally accessible characterization of steady-state reorganization.
summary: This work introduces the geometric phase as a universal diagnostic tool for understanding steady-state reorganization in driven-dissipative quantum oscillators. By analyzing the phase winding protocol, the authors show that the GP captures critical phenomena like phase locking and dissipative phase transitions. This method is highly valuable because it probes the entire eigensystem structure, offering a more comprehensive view than traditional observables.
main_problem: The paper aims to find a unified geometric diagnostic to characterize steady-state reorganization in driven-dissipative quantum oscillators, linking phase locking and dissipative phase transitions.
main_result: The geometric phase (GP) provides a unified, experimentally accessible diagnostic that captures the reorganization of the steady-state eigensystem across different critical regimes.
method: The analysis utilizes the kinematic geometric phase approach, particularly by winding the drive phase to generate a closed loop of non-equilibrium steady states, reducing the GP to an eigensystem functional.
model_or_system: The study models driven-dissipative bosonic systems, including the Quantum Stuart-Landau (QSL) oscillator and the two-photon-driven Kerr resonator, governed by a master equation.
key_observables: Geometric Phase ($\Gamma_g$), Phase Coherence ($S_q$), and the local geometric response ($\chi_{\Gamma_g}$), which is decomposed into eigenvalue ($\chi_\lambda$) and eigenvector ($\chi_n$) contributions.
important_parameters: Drive strengths ($E, \eta$), damping rates ($\gamma_1, \gamma_2, \kappa$), and the proximity to critical points like the Hopf threshold.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on perturbative expansions in the weak-drive limit, and for measurement, it employs mixed-state interferometry (Ramsey sequence) to bypass full density matrix reconstruction.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the perturbative GP response showing Arnold-tongue behavior, the GP near the Hopf threshold showing nonperturbative reorganization, and the decomposition of the GP response across first and second-order transitions in the Kerr resonator.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the general geometric phase for nonunitary evolution, applying it to the QSL oscillator to show its connection to phase locking, and finally analyzing the Kerr resonator to decompose the response into eigenvalue and eigenvector contributions near phase transitions.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, unified geometric tool to diagnose complex non-equilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems, moving beyond simple mean-field observables to probe the underlying structure of the steady-state eigensystem.
